the effect of SWD on tomato fruit quality is more evident under a Mediterranean climate than in a temperate climate.
the effects of soil water deficit during fruit development and maturation on fruit firmness, soluble solids and total solids are more evident than on fruit yield.

the development of a deficit irrigation strategy to improve fruit quality and to increase water use efficiency of processing tomato under the Mediterranean climate.
the effect of SWD on yield and quality in processing tomato under a deficit irrigation regime, and with the influence of site characteristics on the response of fruit quality.
a new approach to deficit irrigation of processing tomato, in which the SWD was imposed during the whole fruit development and ripeness.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of soil water deficit depend on the specific crop, the environmental conditions and the specific traits considered.
the quality traits of processing tomatoes can be improved under deficit irrigation, but only if water is saved without compromising yield.

, in order to achieve the maximum water savings in processing tomato production under a Mediterranean climate, the irrigation regime should be adjusted according to the crop water requirements, and that the irrigation period should be extended until the end of ripening.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in order to maintain a constant fruit quality, it is possible to reduce irrigation up to 50% ET0, with a saving of 47% water.

the effects of SWD on yield and fruit quality of processing tomato are strongly dependent on the environmental conditions in which the crop is grown, and that the best compromise between yield and fruit quality can be obtained by applying deficit irrigation during the fruiting stage.
the effects of SWD on fruit firmness are more important than on fruit size and quality.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in order to obtain a tomato product with a good quality, it is necessary to irrigate the crop at a high rate during the fruit development phase, and then to reduce the irrigation rate during the ripening phase.
the effects of SWD on tomato quality are not only related to SWD but also to other soil and climatic conditions.
it is possible to produce processing tomato under SWD without a significant loss in quality, and that it is possible that the quality of tomato grown under deficit irrigation may even be improved.
